GOAL: check each of the four proposals against the shared frozen bundle (same E1-E13 for all four bundles: bundles 8bef1936fe52fe0d, 59d5537a06b2c42e, c533b1153c3faa6e, 3a34d4b40fe8f322 are identical in their OBSERVED rows).
READ: E5 (successor-entropy stratification: top-1 mass 0.4375 in lowest-entropy quintile vs 0.0543 in highest, rho=-0.973; mean distinct successors 2.72/4.54/6.60/10.84/41.41 across quintiles), E6/E7 (width-20 beam survival and per-position NLL), E8 (first-level capacity ceiling: K=16 share 0.3106 vs K=256 0.0822), E9 (cohort-profile: positive shares a successor cohort 0.9291 vs 0.8871 negatives; profile overlap beats all 10 negatives in 0.5898 of pairs), E10 (edge_density 5.33, mean out-degree 5.45, distinct_edges 115582), E11 (same_first_prefix_rate 0.0907 vs permuted null 0.067).
OBSERVED LEVER: every existing arm is below the 0.065 target: l1_br 0.04671, l1_br_euclid 0.06207, l1_only 0.06233, resample 0.06363 (best), successor_entropy 0.05122, successor_geodesic_coarse 0.05500, successor_geodesic_coarse_v2 0.05463, tangent_successor_residual 0.05500. So the required delta is only ~+0.0014 over resample but ~+0.003 over the Euclidean-assignment baseline.
REASONING: (i) assignment-preserving / plain-Euclidean-prefix arms (0.062-0.0636) beat every geometry-flavoured arm (0.051-0.055), so a mechanism that keeps the Euclidean assignment and only edits the estimator has the best evidence support; (ii) SIDs are near-unique (l1_br gold prefix alive 1.000/1.000/1.000/0.068 with recall 0.0467) so level-1/2 prefix sharing is already saturated in at least one arm, while collision pressure (E11 barely above null) makes forced closeness at level L dangerous; (iii) E5/E9 show the behaviour structure is real and coarse (64 cohorts carry signal), which supports a *mild* behaviour-weighted code relocation, not a new metric.
STILL OPEN: which of the two Karcher-estimator proposals is first (scope of change and constant derivation), and whether the mixed-curvature product's behaviour statistic is measured anywhere.`});
const step2 = await tools.progress.append_progress({content: `STAGE 2 - per-proposal placement
GOAL: derive the total order from the Stage-1 levers.
READ (against each bundle): SUCC-GEO-CBTAB E12/E13 (curvature kappa=1/s^2, s^2 = mean ||zhat||^2 measured at end of epoch 0 - derived, good) but its CHANGE/SPEC give a softplus triplet margin with NO margin value and NO loss coefficient relative to the RQ-VAE objective, i.e. two free constants that the policy forbids tuning; its stated observables are level-1/level-2 successor prefix hit rate, a dimension that E6/E7 already show is saturated (1.000/1.000 at depths 1-2 for l1_br) while the actual loss is at depth 4 (0.068); and E6 shows the successor-geodesic family lost (0.0550/0.0546/0.0550 vs 0.0621 Euclidean).
BFRQ-KARCHER-MASS E12/E13: geometry acts only in code estimation, "Assignment code path, encoder, decoder, loss and Stage 3 are untouched" - the only proposal whose footprint respects the observed ranking of arms in E6; constants are data-derived (tau = median||z|| measured once, c=1 unit, eta_k=1/(1+N_k) assignment-count damping, 99th-pct clip); cost +1-3% Stage 2. Weakness: w_i = 1+log1p(mu) is mild so it may be inert (its own risk) and the Karcher mean contracts codes toward the centre.
poincare-frechet-successor-codebook: also estimator-level but additionally moves the assignment into Poincare distance and weights the commitment term, i.e. it adds two geometry-on-the-assignment surfaces that E6 shows are the losing family; eta=1 hard jump with ~1023 items/step over 3x256 codes (~4 points/cell, E10 mean out-degree 5.45 shows cells are sparse) is noisier than BFRQ's damped step; weights (indeg+1)/(n_v+2) clipped [0.25,4] then batch-normalised do guarantee a 16x spread, so it will fire where BFRQ may not. Cost +5-10% vs +1-3%.
MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ: the gating statistic (directed local clustering coefficient C_i) is NOT measured anywhere in the bundle (E10 reports only edge counts/out-degree, nothing on cycles among successors); the fix sets g_i=0.5 when k_i<5 and E5 gives mean distinct successors 2.72 and 4.54 for the two lowest quintiles, so ~40% of items sit on the default and the mechanism is inert for them; it also adds two trainable curvatures plus a spherical fibre that "the decoder may ignore" (its own risk) and puts curvature back into the assignment metric. Its constants are at least documented defaults, so it is more policy-compliant than SUCC-GEO-CBTAB.
CONCLUSION: order = BFRQ-KARCHER-MASS > poincare-frechet-successor-codebook > MIXCURV-FIBRE-RQ > SUCC-GEO-CBTAB. Placed BFRQ first on the E6 arm ordering (Euclidean-assignment/prefix arms 0.0621-0.0636 vs geometry arms 0.0510-0.0550) plus fully derived constants and the smallest footprint; poincare-frechet second because its stronger, batch-normalised weight spread will actually fire but its curved assignment+commitment re-introduces the losing surface; MIXCURV third on an unmeasured behaviour statistic and a ~40% inert default (E5); SUCC-GEO-CBTAB last because its two constants (margin, loss scale) are unspecified/tunable in violation of the no-tuning policy and its lever targets the already-saturated level-1/2 prefixes (E6/E7) while pushing level-L SIDs together risks the near-unique SID space (E11).
STILL OPEN: none; single run, no ablation arm, no tuning - the placement uses only recorded evidence.`});
return [step1, step2];
